content: A blood cell, also referred to as a blood corpuscle, is any type of cell that is typically present in the blood. In mammals, blood cells are categorized into three main types: red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. Collectively, these three types of blood cells constitute approximately 45% of the blood tissue, with the remaining 55% being plasma. A reduction in the number of blood cells is termed cytopenia, while an increase in the number of blood cells is referred to as polycythemia.
